uart.signal: real PlatformIO-compiled Arduino firmware; the sim captures hardware UART0/USARTx bytes and a uart_contains oracle matches the LW_L0_OK marker printed from setup()
uart.lane: core-arduino-matrix-smoke / arduino-matrix-gate (nightly 02:20 UTC + push to main)
uart.note: firmware_survival.rs also has an nrf52832_demo case, but its expected_uart_output is b"" and assert_uart_contains short-circuits on an empty expectation - that case proves nothing about UART.

spi.gap: SPIM EasyDMA is STARTed and EVENTS_END/TXD.AMOUNT/RXD.AMOUNT are checked - counts, not content. It never compares SPI_RX_BUF against SPI_TX_BUF, so it cannot tell a transferred byte from garbage.
spi.lane: core-ci / core-full (nightly 02:30 UTC + workflow_dispatch + '[full-ci]') via tier1_matrix + tier1_matrix_ratchet

i2c.signal: real Arduino firmware writes a register-pointer byte to the INA219 model attached at 0x40 in validation/arduino-matrix/systems/<chip>.yaml and Wire.endTransmission() returns 0 (the device ACKed); the verdict LW_L3_OK then comes back as real bytes on the modelled UART, matched by a uart_contains oracle
i2c.lane: core-arduino-matrix-smoke / arduino-matrix-gate (nightly 02:20 UTC + push to main)
i2c.note: the ACK is meaningful because the same chips' tier-1 fixtures show an UNMATCHED address NACKs (esp32 check_i2c addr 0x20, stm32 NACKF, rp2040 ABRT_7B_ADDR_NOACK) - the bus does not blanket-ACK. LIMIT: this proves address+data out and the device's ACK back, not a payload readback. Evidence: run 30842505709, 'cells=45 expected>=45 fails=0', 2026-08-03.
